hero.title: Worldline
hero.summary:
Worldline is the European leader in payment services and secure transactions. Within the bench team, I contribute to the design and development of WL Benchmark, a multi-tenant internal observability platform built to compare performance between two releases or two time periods, detect anomalies and forecast trends with Machine Learning.
The priority use case: automating the generation of CR Bench reports, previously written by hand, by crossing local Gatling data with GCP Cloud Monitoring dashboards. The platform relies on a project-agnostic core and per-tenant configuration so it can adapt to each team without code changes.
The details and deliverables are confidential because the project is internal to Worldline. The project is still in progress — feel free to ask me any questions about it.

hero.title: DocHub
hero.summary: DocHub is a distributed appointment-booking platform built as part of an introductory DevOps course. The application is based on five independently containerized services — a PostgreSQL database, a FastAPI API, a Vue.js frontend, an Nginx reverse proxy, and a Python worker for batch processing — orchestrated with Docker, including dependency management and ordered healthchecks. A GitHub Actions pipeline automates building and pushing images to GitHub Container Registry, then runs two test suites. The project implements key DevOps practices: reproducible YAML configuration, non-root containers, infrastructure-as-code, automated testing, and orchestration.

meta.label: Type
meta.value: Distributed appointment-booking platform, introducing DevOps, CI/CD and YAML

hero.title: Music Story
hero.summary: Music Story is a professional provider of music metadata and enrichment services for B2B players: media, platforms, and rights holders. I contributed to the redesign of their showcase website by upgrading a heterogeneous WordPress base to a more modern Next.js platform built on reusable components and shipped iteratively, with code reviews alongside the team. The redesign made the site faster and more consistent, fully internationalized and better referenced, while simplifying maintenance and speeding up the creation of new pages.

hero.title: Paris 92
hero.summary:
Paris 92 is a women’s handball club recognized on the national and European scene that wants to optimize how it manages and analyzes its data.
I contributed to the design and implementation of a secure platform centralizing match data, videos, and physical metrics, in collaboration with five students from ISEN. My role: versatile front/back developer with a Next.js interface and a Python back-end for data processing.
The platform lets coaches, analysts, and trainers track workload, compare performance, prepare for matches, and generate reports in a few clicks — streamlining collaboration, making information gathering more reliable, and speeding up decision-making.
Code and deliverables are confidential, but you can ask me about them.

hero.title: MedChem Structure Genius
hero.summary:
MedChem Structure Genius is an e-learning application designed for students at the University of Lille Faculty of Pharmacy to help them study molecules and their relationships.
In collaboration with a team of five ISEN students, I led this project by scoping needs with the client, running weekly meetings, and ensuring follow-up while contributing directly to development.
We improved the reliability and usability of the app: fixing display bugs on Android and the web, resolving quiz-generation errors, reworking the review and score-tracking interfaces, optimising the code, correcting texts, and creating a diagram that explains the quiz-generation mechanism and typical Supabase queries to make data exploration easier.

meta.value: Development of a web and mobile e-learning application on drug structure
